R058-01.notes: Passage moves from old account to 2002 revision to tearless onions. D covers only para 5, C misreads the garlic comparison, A has no advocacy.

R058-02.notes: Para 2: the second enzyme converts the intermediate into the volatile irritant. A describes alliinase, which is the trap.

R058-03.notes: 'The trouble was...' marks an anomaly for the older account. B contradicts the passage, which says alliinase does the same work in garlic.

R058-04.notes: The enzyme takes hold of the intermediate before it self-reacts. 'Attacks suddenly' and 'confiscates' are tempting but carry the wrong connotation.

R058-05.notes: Para 3: the intermediate might follow the garlic-like path. B tempts with the idea of more sulfur compounds, but the passage says alliinase output is unchanged and only its fate is rerouted.

R058-06.notes: Close to verbatim. D misplaces the bred onion in New Zealand.

R058-07.notes: The sentence limits the claim: the tricks reduce the irritant but do not stop the reaction. A overstates it as dismissal.

R058-08.notes: A sharp knife works by breaking fewer cells, so less starting material is released. Fewer, cleaner cuts also break fewer cells. A works by slowing the reaction, B and D by keeping the irritant from reaching the eyes. I checked whether C could be a weak extrapolation; it still holds as the single best answer.

R058-09.notes: Para 6: the chemistry is a defense against animals, and its effect on cooks is incidental.

R058-10.notes: Cutting ruptures cells so the enzyme meets the sulfur compounds. B is a later step, D is garlic's path, and C comes after the irritant forms.

R058-11.notes: 'Until the light went thin' means fading daylight, so faint. A and C are the literal physical senses.

R058-12.notes: 'Would come out smaller than it was.' The other options have no support.

R058-13.notes: First-person narrator who was fourteen, lives on the street, and watches from a window, looking back. Calling the narrator a 'neighbor' is a fair inference.

fact_check: All checked claims are accurate or acceptably simplified: the alliinase-only model held for roughly three decades before Imai et al. (House Foods), Nature 2002; LFS turns 1-propenesulfenic acid into syn-propanethial-S-oxide; in garlic, 2-propenesulfenic acid self-condenses to allicin; Crop & Food Research (New Zealand) and House Foods (Japan) suppressed LFS by RNA interference around 2008, raised thiosulfinate levels, and never sold those onions; House Foods' non-GM tearless onion (Smile Ball) reached stores in Japan around 2015; the kitchen tricks are explained reasonably. A minor point that needs no flag: the commercial onion reportedly lowers irritant output by a different route (lower alliinase activity, from mutation breeding), but the passage claims only that it 'produce[s] little of the irritant', which is accurate.
